name: Wenaas Lars
forbes_bio: Lars Wenaas is the owner of Wenaasgruppen, a hotel property empire with 18 hotels and 7,800 rooms across Europe.
Wenaasgruppen also manages a portfolio of listed stocks and bonds through its financial investment arm.
Wenaas began in the family's workwear business before shifting to hotel real estate investments in the 1990s.
The group has acquired or developed over 58 hotels, including Radisson Blu Plaza in Oslo and hotels in Copenhagen.

name: Jonas Kleberg
forbes_bio: Jonas Kleberg is the Chairman and CEO of Soya Group, a multi-billion dollar Swedish family conglomerate.
He is the grandson of Olof Wallenius, who founded the group in 1934.
The family's wealth stems primarily from shipping, including a major stake in Wallenius Wilhelmsen, one of the world's largest car carriers.
Under Kleberg's leadership, the group has diversified into real estate, wind-propulsion technology, and forestry.
He and his sister, Annika Bootmans Kleberg, each own 50% of the Soya Group, which also includes a trotting horse breeding operation.
forbes_facts: The family company is named "Soya" because the founder's first vessels in the 1930s were converted to carry soybean oil, a pioneering move at the time.

name: Martin Lavoo
forbes_bio: Martin Lavoo is a grandson of the late Singaporean paints tycoon Goh Cheng Liang, who died in August 2025 at age 98.
The Goh family draws the bulk of its wealth from a majority stake in Japan's Nippon Paint Holdings, one of the world's largest paint manufacturers.
Martin, together with his brother and four cousins, inherited the bulk of their grandfather's fortune.

His mother is Chiat Jin, the only daughter of the late patriarch who started making paints in a small factory in Singapore before partnering with Nippon Paint in 1962. His uncle, Hup Jin, is the chairman of Nippon Paint.
In 2013, Martin cofounded Sustenir Agriculture, an urban farming enterprise in Singapore.

name: Zhou Yahui
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Zhou Yahui is the founder and director of Beijing Kunlun Tech, a Beijing-headquartered operator of online games. He stepped down as chairman in April 2020 to focus on his African mobile payment business, Opay.
Zhou's former wife Li Qiong became a billionaire in 2016 following the couple's divorce settlement.
Zhou holds a master's degree from China's elite Tsinghua University.

name: Ingrid Wu
forbes_bio: Ingrid Wu is a co-founder of Shenzhen-headquartered electronics manufacturer AAC Technologies; her husband Benjamin Pan is the CEO.
Wu is a non-executive director and not involved in the day-to-day operations, according to the company.
AAC went public at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2005.
Wu is a graduate of the Changzhou School of Public Health in China.
Wu is the mother of Kelvin Pan, an executive vice president at AAC and the company's chief innovation officer.

name: Turgay Ciner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2002-2023); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Turgay Ciner (pronounced "jin-ner"), who worked as an errand boy in tea shops during high school, presides over a fortune built on soda ash.
Soda ash is used in glass, detergents and various industrial products. Ciner's Eti Soda and Kazan Soda are among the world's top producers.
In 2025, Ciner's London-based WE Soda acquired U.S. producer Genesis Alkali for $1.4 billion, reinforcing its position as the world's largest natural soda ash producer.
Ciner sold his media empire -- including Habertürk, Show TV and Bloomberg HT -- at the end of 2024, ending a 22-year run as one of Turkey's most prominent media owners.
Ciner's Silopi Electric, in Turkey's Southeastern Anatolia region, generates power from thermal plants fueled by coal extracted from Ciner mines.
forbes_facts: Turgay Ciner and his brother imported autos from Germany and had a shop in Istanbul Talimhane, now site of the modern headquarters building of Ciner Publishing.

name: Richard Kayne
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Richard Kayne cofounded alternative asset manager Kayne Anderson Capital Advisors.
The $33 billion (assets under management) company is the largest investor in energy pipelines in the United States.
Kayne began his career as an analyst in New York in the mid 1960s then managed money at financial services firm Cantor Fitzgerald.
He launched Kayne Anderson in 1984 and remains its co-chairman.

name: Derek Stevens
forbes_bio: Derek Stevens is the CEO and majority owner of three casinos in Downtown Las Vegas, The Golden Gate, The D and his crown jewel, Circa.
Stevens, who co-owns these properties with his brother, opened Circa in October 2020 at a cost of $1 billion. It was the first new casino in Downtown Las Vegas since the 1980s.
Born in Grosse Point, Michigan, Stevens is also the CEO of Cold Heading Co., a leading manufacturer and supplier of fasteners for the auto industry that his family started in the early 1900s.
Stevens first bought 50% of The Golden Gate on Fremont Street, which opened in 1906 as Sin City's first hotel and casino. A few years later, he bought the rest.
In 2011, Stevens bought Fitzgerald's, an Irish-themed casino, and completed a 36-story renovation and renamed it The D.
Stevens also owns Circa Sports, a sports betting company that is live across seven states.

name: Zhong Naixiong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2017-2025); Hurun China (2016-2024)
forbes_bio: Zhong Naixiong is founder and chairman of Nenking Group, a conglomerate headquartered in the southern Chinese city of Foshan.
Nenking's business include international trade, financial investment, real estate, sports events and pharmaceuticals.
